headline: Approved June 4, 2026 minutes and raised no objection to a CRMC swim float application at 257 Walmsley Ln.
summary: The Waterfront Advisory Commission reviewed old business including the Harbor Management Plan, GIS mapping of shoreline access, boat storage rights-of-way, hydrilla treatment, and the Narrow River boat ramp project. The commission approved prior meeting minutes and voted not to object to a CRMC swim float application at 257 Walmsley Ln.
decisions: Voted that the Commission does not object to the CRMC swim float application at 257 Walmsley Ln, 5-0.

decision_evidence.quote: Motion by C. Duckworth to approve June 4, 2026 minutes. Seconded by J. Nuzzolillo. Motion passed 5-0.
C. Duckworth made a motion that the Commission does not have an objection to the application as presented. B. Gross seconded. Motion passed 5-0.

A. Call to Order & Roll Call
Town of South Kingstown
Waterfront Advisory Commission
Regular Session Meeting Minutes
Thursday, August 6, 2026 at 7:00 PM
The Neighborhood Guild
325 Columbia St., Peace Dale, RI
www.southkingstownri.gov
Meeting called to order by S. Grimley at 7:04pm
B. Approval of Minutes:
June 4, 2026
Michael Sherry, Chairman
Connor Duckworth
Motion by C. Duckworth to approve June 4, 2026 minutes. Seconded by J. Nuzzolillo. Motion passed 5-0.
C. Correspondence & Public Comment:
1. Narragansett Harbor Commission Agenda / Minutes
Provided to members for ex officio status.
D. Old Business:
1. Harbor Management Plan Update
Samuel Grimley
Barry Gross
Sara Mariani
Nathaniel Merrill
Joseph Nuzzolillo
M. Stach provided the most recent correspondence from DEM attorney to the Solicitors' office. Brian Wagner, Deputy
Town Planner and Solicitor's office, is working on a response to DEM. Water Quality Certificate is the last piece needed
before Town Council adoption.
2. Development of Online GIS Based Map Showing South Kingstown Rights of Way to Shore
Tracey Owens, Principle Planner for South Kingstown, showed the members her work on developing a GIS-based
mapping program to show the public coastal access points in South Kingstown and solicited feedback on the properties
and design that the members would like to see.
3. Public Right-of Way Access at Locations 10 and 11. Re: Boats and Waterways Ordinance 4-14: Rights-of-Way
to the Water - Boat Storage
PA Site 10: Washington Street, Location: Matunuck, Water Area: Segar Cove, Assessor's Plat: 87-4,
Recorded Plat: LE34/78
Waiting on CRMC permit.
4. Boats and Waterways Ordinance Revisions / Updates
Members will work on this as time allows.
5. Coastal Road and Public Right-of Way to the Water Survey and Monumentation; Charlestown Beach Road
Survey Status
Staff working to complete work to send out to bid.
6. Expansion of Parking Lot at Marina Park West Lot to Accommodate Increased Seasonal Activity
The Parks Department will be replacing the post and rail fence and adding post and rail to the east side of the lot along
the newly planted grass. Signage and divider fence will also be added as time allows.
7. Marina Park / Town Farm Park Master Plan w/Connectivity to Downtown Wakefield
Staff will look into whether this project can begin with the partial funding that has been received.
8. Formerly Leased Waterfront Area Along Saugatucket River Adjacent to Marina Park Green Space -
Returning to Town Operations July 1, 2027
Members will work on recommendations to the Town Council for use of this area.
9. Development of Indian Lake Management Plan (June 25, 2026 6:30pm Public Meeting at Town Hall)
Public meeting held with contractor working on the plan. Project moving forward.
10. Planned Development of a Saugatucket River Watershed Plan by RIDEM
RIDEM to work on this project.
11. Hydrilla
M. Stach reported that the town is completing its final year of treatment of hydrilla at Indian Lake, funded by a RIDEM
BWRF grant. RIDEM has secured some funding from SNEP for next years treatment but the balance will need to come
from other sources. Greaters are working at the boat ramps, hired by RIDEM.
Funding has been secured to begin treatment of hydrilla at Worden Pond. RIDEM secured funds from USDA for one year
of treatment.
12. Reconstruction of RIDEM Narrow River Boat Ramp @ Mitchell and Pollock Ave
M. Stach reported that there has been new correspondence between DEM and NRPA relating to some legal work on the
ownership issues of the site. The town has a meeting scheduled for August 26, 2026 to discuss some of the titling and
property issues with the site.
E. New Business:
1. New Harbormaster Boat Christening - August 19, 2026 @ 12:30pm
Christening Ceremony scheduled for August 19th at 12:30. All are invited.
2. CRMC Application for State Assent-Swim Float-257 Walmsley Ln
M. Stach presented a CRMC application for a swim float adjacent to a private property on the Narrow River. CRMC has a
process to administratively approve this without going through the 30-day public comment. Presented to the
Commission for their review to provide feedback to CRMC if necessary.
After review of location and potential effects on navigation, seeing none more than a boat on a mooring would present,
C. Duckworth made a motion that the Commission does not have an objection to the application as presented. B. Gross
seconded. Motion passed 5-0.
F. Harbormaster's Report:
NBMTF and Harbor Safety Committee Town Council - New Boat New Vessel Security Coverage of Station Pt. Judith
AOR for RB-S During Sail 250 USCG Sector - New Boat Blessing of the Fleet USCGC Eagle Matunuck Surf Shop
Paddle Board Race
M. Stach provided updates on NBMTF meeting, Harbor Safety meeting, the new boat and its updated role in the area,
recent response and activity, and upcoming marine events in town.
G. Next Meeting:
September 3, 2026
September 3, 2026
H. Adjournment:
Motion to adjourn at 8:16pm by B. Gross, seconded by J. Nuzzolillo. Motion passed 5-0
